Definition: from G5408; a murderer (always of criminal (or at least intentional) homicide; which G443 does not necessarily imply; while G4607 is a special term for a public bandit):--murderer.
BiblicalUsage: Phoneus is a murderer, and Scripture names him where the charge is sharpest. Peter tells the crowd they denied the Holy One and desired a murderer to be granted to them, and Stephen charges that the fathers became the betrayers and murderers of the Just One. Peter warns believers not to suffer as a murderer or a thief, and John lists murderers among those whose part is in the lake of fire.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the murderer in the Bible is never an abstraction: the crowd chose Barabbas over Jesus, the fathers killed the prophets, and the lake of fire waits for the unrepentant. Yet the same Scriptures say the murderer can be forgiven, because the blood of Christ was shed for murderers too. My position is that the charge against me is real, and so is the pardon.
